title: Nairobi Sets Two-Week Push to Complete Priority Flood Works
desc: Nairobi has given county and KURA teams two weeks to accelerate drainage and road works in areas repeatedly affected by flooding.
content:
Nairobi County and the Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) have been directed to accelerate critical drainage and road works within the next 14 days as the city prepares for anticipated El Niño rains.

Governor Johnson Sakaja issued the directive on Thursday, September 24, during a meeting with KURA Director-General Eng. Silas Kinoti, county and KURA engineers and contractors at Barabara Plaza in Nairobi.

The teams have been told to give priority to roads and neighbourhoods that repeatedly experience flooding whenever heavy rains hit the capital.

Sakaja said the remaining window before the rains intensify should be used to speed up ongoing interventions in areas identified as vulnerable to flooding. He called for closer coordination between county and national government agencies working on Nairobi's road and drainage infrastructure.

The governor said the focus should be on practical works capable of reducing flood risks rather than treating the projects as routine maintenance.

KURA has also committed to intensifying drainage works. Kinoti said engineers had been assigned specific areas and that the required interventions would be undertaken within the two-week period.

The immediate works are expected to focus on drainage infrastructure and roads in areas where flooding has repeatedly disrupted movement and affected residents.

The directive comes as Nairobi continues broader preparations for the expected rains. Authorities have been clearing and improving drainage channels and waterways in different parts of the city, while agencies responsible for roads, disaster response and waterways have been coordinating preparedness efforts.

The Nairobi Rivers Commission has separately reported ongoing drainage clearance in areas including parts of Westlands, Eastlands, Starehe, South C, Dagoretti and Embakasi Central. This includes work to clear blocked drainage channels and improve stormwater flow.

The national government is also accelerating flood-mitigation measures in Nairobi. Deputy President Kithure Kindiki said on Thursday that agencies had been directed to fast-track drainage clearance, dredging and other interventions, while temporary safe grounds have been identified in case residents in unsafe areas need to relocate.

For Nairobi residents, the immediate concern is whether the ongoing works can be completed before heavy rains put pressure on the city's drainage and road networks.

The 14-day directive therefore places emphasis on completing priority interventions quickly, particularly in neighbourhoods where flooding has become a recurring problem.
